Heard the arguments of learned counsel for the appellants and learned High Court Government Pleader for respondent-State.
3.
The appellants are accused Nos.1 to 3 before the trial Court and the respondent is prosecution.
The rank of the parties is retained for the sake of convenience.

The case of prosecution is that on the complaint of P.W.2-Amaravva filed on 22.01.2014, the Lingasugur police registered FIR in Crime No.37/2014 as per Ex.P.13 against accused Nos.1 to 5 for the offences punishable under Sections 143, 147, 366(A) read with Section 149 of IPC, where the complainant has alleged in her complaint as per Ex.P.2 that her daughter (victim girl), aged about 16 years, is studying in I PUC and on 20.01.2014 at 9.40 a.m., when she was going to college, accused Nos.1 to 5 (accused Nos.4 and 5 not charge sheeted) said to be abducted the victim girl in an auto rickshaw which was seen by P.W.4- Ramanna and P.W.5- Bheemappa and they intimated to her.
Hence, she lodged the complaint for abduction of her daughter by the appellants and other two persons.
The police registered the FIR for the aforesaid offences.

5. Subsequently, on 26.01.2014, P.W.1-victim appeared before the police and given a statement as per NC: 2023:KHC-K:8756 Ex.P.1 stating that she herself voluntarily went with the appellant-accused on 20.01.2014 and nobody forced her and both of them went to Mumbai to the Mallesh @ Mallu S/O Manappa Rathod vs The State Of Karnataka on 18 November, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/37525839/
3 house of accused No.1 and on 21.01.2014, both of the stayed together and appellant-accused No.1 said to be had sexual intercourse with her stating that he has already married her and he was her husband.

sentences.text: Subsequently, she came to know that her mother lodged the complaint.
Hence, the accused persons brought her to the police station.
She has stated that the accused never abducted her.

After receipt of the statement from the P.W.1, once again, the police registered FIR by adding Section 376 of IPC and Section 4 of Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012 (hereafter "POCSO Act").

sentences.text: 6. The accused No.1 was arrested on 27.01.2014 and he was remanded to judicial custody.

Subsequently, the police filed charge sheet for the offences punishable under Sections 376, 366A read with Section 34 of IPC and Section 4 of POCSO Act and dropped the charge sheet NC:
2023:KHC-K:8756 against accused No.4 and 5 along with the offences punishable under Sections 143, 147, read with Section 149 of IPC.
The Special Court being the POCSO Court took cognizance and framed charges for the offences punishable under Sections 376, 366A read with Section 34 of IPC and Section 4 of POCSO Act.
The accused denied the charges and claimed to be tried.
Accordingly, the prosecution examined 12 witnesses and got marked 16 documents and no material objects were marked.
The statement under Section 313 of Cr.P.C. was recorded and incriminating evidence was read over to the accused persons.
The case of the accused was one of the total denial and not chosen to enter the witness box or examine any witnesses.

7. After hearing the arguments, the trial Court found the appellants guilty and convicted as under:
(a) The appellant-accused No.1 was sentenced to undergo simple imprisonment for 10 years and to pay fine of Rs.25,000/- for the offence punishable under Section 376 of IPC.

He was further sentenced to undergo simple imprisonment for 10 years and to pay fine of Rs.5,000/- for the offence punishable under Section 366-A of IPC.
He was also sentenced to undergo simple imprisonment for 7 years and to pay fine of Rs.5,000/- for the offence punishable under Section 4 of POCSO Act.
were sentenced to undergo simple imprisonment for 3 years and to pay fine of Rs.5,000/- each for the offence punishable under Section 336-A of IPC with default sentences.
Being aggrieved by the same, the appellants are before this Court.

8. Learned counsel for the appellants has strenuously contended that the judgment of the trial Court is erroneous in passing the impugned judgment, wherein the trial Court has not considered the evidence of P.W.1, who has given statement as per Ex.P.1 stating that nobody abducted her and she voluntarily went, and also NC: 2023:KHC-K:8756 that P.W.1 has given the contradictory evidence before the Court that the accused persons abducted her, this aspect was not considered.
It is further contended that the age of the victim was more than 18 years and she was studied up to PUC.

The investigation officer has not collected any evidence and examined the Principal to prove that the age of the victim was below 18 years, though examined the doctors and dentist as well as the radiologist,
but it is not conclusive proof for proving the age of the victim that she was below the age of 18 years.

sentences.text: It is further contended by the learned counsel that, even otherwise, the doctor-P.W.10 has clearly stated that there is no recent sexual intercourse, and the FSL report has also not depicted any seminal stains on the cloth or body of the victim.

These are all going to suggest that there is no evidence against the accused persons for committing any of the offences, but the trial Court committed the error in convicting the appellants and hence, prayed for allowing the appeals and to acquit the appellants.

Per contra, learned High Court Government Pleader supported the judgment of the trial Court and contended that as regards the age of the victim, Ex.P.16 as well as the evidence of P.W.12 clearly goes to show that her age was below 18 years and the doctors-P.Ws.8 and 9 also stated that her age was below 18 years.
P.Ws.4 and 5 have seen the accused persons abducting the victim girl.
The mother of the victim also filed a complaint for abduction.
Even otherwise, the victim has given consent for going along with the accused, but that cannot be considered as a valid consent as she is a minor, and her consent and willingness is immaterial.

Therefore, it is contended that there is sufficient material placed on record and based upon the same, the trial Court has rightly convicted the appellants and hence, prayed for dismissing the appeal.
10. Having heard the arguments of learned counsel for the parties, perused the records.

The points that arise for my consideration are as under :
(i) Whether the prosecution proves beyond reasonable doubt that on 20.01.2014 at 9.40 a.m., the accused Nos.1 to 3 abducted the victim minor girl, aged about 17 years, from the lawful guardianship, by compelling her for sexual intercourse and compelling her for marriage, thereby,
they committed the offence punishable under Section 366-A of IPC ?
(ii) Whether the prosecution further proves that accused No.1 committed sexual assault on the victim, against her will, on 21.01.2014 and thereby, he has committed an offence punishable under Section 376 of IPC read with Section 4 of POCSO Act ?
(iii) Whether the judgment of conviction and the order of sentence passed by the trial Court calls for any interference ?
12. Before going to the appreciation of evidence on record, it is worth to mention the evidence adduced by the prosecution before the trial Court.
As stated above, the prosecution in all examined 12 witnesses.

P.W.1 is the victim girl, aged about 17 years.

She has deposed that on 20.01.2014 (Monday) at 9.40 a.m., when she was going to the college, at that time, three accused persons along with two other accused persons i.e., Savitha and Amaresh, came and gagged her mouth with cloth and something smeared on the face and she became unconscious.
Later, she gained conscious at 8.00 a.m. on the next day, where she came to know that she was in Mumbai.
Later, accused No.1 said to be forced her to lie down, otherwise, he will kill her.
The other accused persons also forced her and they bolted the room and accused No.1 sexually assaulted her by force.
On 26.01.2014, all the accused persons brought her to Lingsugur police station and on the force of the accused, she has given information/statement as per Ex.P.1.

this witness has been treated as hostile by the public prosecutor and she was subjected to cross examination by the public prosecutor where the public prosecutor, suggested that she has given the statement before the - 12 - NC: 2023:KHC-K:8756 police as per Ex.P.5 and she has denied.

In the cross examination of learned counsel for the accused, P.W.1 has stated that while she was going to the college, there were so many students passing on the said place and she has admitted that she has not given statement to the police that the accused persons gagged her mouth and smeared some powder on the face, thereby she became unconscious.
She further denied that the accused persons not abducted her, but she has voluntarily went with them.
She also denied that she is deposing false.

14. P.W.2- Amaravva, who is the mother of the victim, has stated that on 20.01.2014, P.Ws.4 and 5 came and informed that her daughter was abducted by the accused persons and she tried to search her, but could not found and hence, she lodged the complaint to police as per Ex.P.2 and she has stated that the age of victim was 16 years.
She has further deposed that after 5-6 days, the police informed her that her victim daughter was found.
Then she came to know that the accused had taken her - 13 - NC: 2023:KHC-K:8756 daughter to Mumbai and sexually assaulted her.
She has further stated that while going to Mumbai, the victim was wearing two tolas of gold chain.
She has also stated that she has not given any further statement to the police.
This witness has also been treated as hostile and she has denied that she has given further statement as per Ex.P.3.

During the cross examination of the learned counsel for the accused, the suggestions that the accused set up defence, P.W.2 was trying to perform the marriage of victim to her own brother Ramanna, the victim was not interested in marrying him and therefore, she eloped with the accused, and the age of the victim was more than 18 years, were all denied by P.W.2.
15.
P.W.3-Amarappa is the panch witness to Ex.P.4.
He has stated that the police asked him to come to the spot where the panchanama was prepared by the police.
In the cross examination, he has denied the suggestion that he has not visited the spot.

Then, they went to P.W.2 and informed the same.
During the cross examination, both of them have admitted that they did not try to prevent the accused from abduction and they denied the suggestion that they were deposing false.
17. P.W.6-Venkatesh is an auto driver and panch witness to Ex.P.6.
He has turned hostile and not supported the prosecution case.
18. P.W.7- Hullappa is the Assistant Sub-inspector.
He has deposed that he went to Mumbai on 08.03.2014 to the house of accused and in the presence of panchas, he prepared panchanama as per Ex.P.6.
He collected the documents in the house of the accused as per Ex.P.7 and - 15 - NC: 2023:KHC-K:8756 returned back, and submitted the report as per Ex.P.8.

In the cross examination, P.W.7 has stated that he has taken the woman police constable along with him and he has not taken the signature of the victim on Ex.P.6, but denied the suggestion that the victim did not show any spot to this witness.

19. On perusal of the evidence, though Ex.P.6 has been signed by two witnesses, but they have not been examined before the Court and even the victim has not signed Ex.P.6 and the victim has also not accompanied by any woman constable.
20. P.W.8 - Dr. Gurushanthappa, a Radiologist from RIMS Hospital, has stated that on 27.01.2014,
he had taken the x-ray of the victim girl regarding estimation of age, and he opined that her age might be between 16 and 17 years and he submitted case sheet as per Ex.P.9 and given opinion as per Ex.P.9-A.
In the cross examination, P.W.8 has admitted that he has not given any separate - 16 - NC: 2023:KHC-K:8756 report regarding the growth of the bones.
He has also admitted that opinion is not inconclusive.

21. P.W.9 - Dr. Amar Varma, who is the Dentist in RIMS Hospital, has deposed that he examined the victim on 27.01.2014 regarding the age, took x-ray and opined that her age was between 15 and 17 years.
He has given opinion as per Ex.P.9-B.

In the cross examination, this witness admitted that there would be chance of finding difference in the teeth and the 3rd molar that would appear in between the age of 18 and 19 years and he has not given any separate opinion in respect of the age.

22. P.W.10 - Dr. Vasima Miya has deposed that he examined the victim on 27.01.2014 and issued a chit as per Ex.P.10 and according to him, after receipt of the FSL report, he has given opinion in Ex.P.11 that there is no signs of recent intercourse on the victim and Ex.P.12 is FSL report.

P.W.11-Khaja Hussain, Police Sub-inspector, received the complaint from P.W.2 on 22.01.2014 and registered FIR in Crime No.37/2013 and also received information from P.W.2 as per Ex.P.2 and FIR has been registered as per Ex.P.13.
He also visited the spot and prepared panchanama as per Ex.P.4 and recorded the statement of C.Ws.5 to 7.
He further deposed that Ex.P.1 was the statement given by the victim.

He handed over further investigation to P.W.12.
24.

P.W.12-Varadaraj, CPI, has deposed that he took up further investigation and sent the victim to medical examination, received opinion of the doctor as per Ex.P.14, recorded further statement of C.Ws.1, 2 and 6.

He also obtained the medical report of accused No.1 as per Ex.P.15, FSL report as per Ex.P.12, the house document of accused as per Ex.P.7 and the age certificate of the victim as per Ex.P.16 and opinion of the doctor as per Ex.P.11.

In the cross examination, this witness has admitted that he has not recorded the statement of any of the persons - 18 - NC: 2023:KHC-K:8756 from the school/college in respect of proving the age of the victim and he has denied the suggestion that the age of the victim is, even though more than 18 years, he has filed a false charge sheet.
25.

On considering the entire evidence on record and perusal of the documents, especially the evidence of P.W.1-victim girl, she has deposed before the Court that, on 20.01.2014, accused Nos.1 to 3 and two others abducted her by gagging her mouth with cloth and smeared some powder on the face and she became unconscious.

Later, she was at Mumbai when she regained conscious and accused No.1 sexually assaulted her and others forced her to lie down with accused No.1.
26.

On perusal of Ex.P.1-complaint given by the victim, she has categorically stated that on 20.01.2014, she herself while going to the college went with accused and no one forced her or abducted her and she fell in love with accused No.1 for last 8 months.
She herself telephoned to accused and asked him to take her.
Accordingly, the accused said to be taken her and married in a temple.

Thereafter, on 21.01.2014, the accused told that she is his wife and therefore, had sexual intercourse Mallesh @ Mallu S/O Manappa Rathod vs The State Of Karnataka on 18 November, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/37525839/
8 with her, whereas in the evidence, she has totally changed her version and stated that the accused persons abducted her by gagging her mouth with cloth and by smearing some powder.
She has admitted that she has not given any statement before the police and the evidence of victim is improved from her previous statement and totally contradicts each other.
27. As per the evidence of P.W.2-hear say witness, P.Ws.4 and 5 came and informed her that the accused abducted the victim in the auto rickshaw.
The auto rickshaw driver has not been examined by the investigation officer and there is no evidence to show that the victim was abducted by the accused in the auto rickshaw.

Though P.Ws.4 and 5 have stated that they have seen the victim while going in the auto rickshaw, but they have not tried to stop or prevented the accused - 20 - NC: 2023:KHC-K:8756 persons from abducting the victim.
On the other hand, the evidence of P.W.1 on Ex.P.1 is altogether contradict each other in respect of abduction or gagging the mouth by the accused persons.

28. As regards the age of victim, P.Ws.8 and 9 have examined the victim and both of them admitted that the age is not conclusive, they have not given separate opinion or separate estimation in respect of development or growth of bones and the possibility of early appearance 3rd molar even after 18 years of age.
Therefore, the evidence of P.Ws.8 and 9 is not sufficient to prove that the age of the victim was below 18 years.
Ex.P.6 produced by the investigation officer where it is stated that date of birth of the victim was 05.12.1987.
The certificate issued by the Principal was not examined by the investigation officer and not examined before the Court by the prosecution to prove that the age of the victim was below 18 years.

Merely marking the document and certificate is not enough and when the victim has stated that she was - 21 - NC: 2023:KHC-K:8756 studying in PUC, the investigation officer was required to obtain the birth certificate or the school certificate or the transfer certificate.
The prosecution has not examined any of the school authorities to prove that the victim was below the age of 18 years.

It appears that taking the doctors' opinion to prove the age, is not conclusive in view of the judgment of the Hon'ble Supreme Court reported in case of JINISH LAL SAW Vs. STATE OF BIHAR reported in 2003 SCC (Criminal) 395.

29. That apart, as regards to sexual assault by accused No.1 on the victim, the evidence of P.W.1-victim contradicts with Ex.P.1 and Ex.P.5.
She has also denied the statement giving before the police as per Ex.P.3.
Further the evidence of Doctor-P.W.10, Exs.P.11 and 12 clearly reveal that there is no spermatozoa detected in any of the articles or items seized by the police.

sentences.text: The evidence of P.W.10 has categorically states that there is no recent sexual intercourse on the victim.

30. If at all the accused took victim girl and sexually assaulted her, within 3-4 days, they would not have come back to Police station and surrendered the victim along with accused before the police.

The victim was subjected to medical examination on the very next date, whereas on the cloth of the victim, vaginal smear and other articles not detected any spermatozoa in order to corroborate the evidence of P.W.1 that she was sexually assaulted by the accused person.
The investigation officer has also not collected any other material to prove the guilt of the accused.

31. Considering the evidence of the victim and her contradictory statement and improved version before the Court, and suppression of her age, college/school - 23 - NC: 2023:KHC-K:8756 certificate, all indicate that the prosecution has not proved the case or guilt of the accused beyond reasonable doubt that on 20.01.2014, the accused persons forcefully abducted the victim, and accused No.1 to 3 compelled her for marriage and accused No.1 sexually assaulted the victim in a house at Mumbai.
No witnesses from Mumbai were examined to show that the accused persons came to Mumbai.
Ex. P.6
- panchanama
is also not proved satisfactorily by the investigation officer.
In a recent judgment, in a similar situation, the Hon'ble Supreme Court, in Criminal Appeal No.1898/2023 decided on 18.07.2023, has acquitted the accused by giving the benefit of doubt.

32. Considering the entire evidence on record, I am of the view that the prosecution has failed to prove the guilt of the accused beyond all reasonable doubt and the trial Court without considering the evidence on record, contradictions and omissions, has convicted the appellant- - 24 - NC: 2023:KHC-K:8756 accused persons for the offences punishable under Section 376 of IPC or Section 4 of POCSO Act.
33. That apart, Section 376 of IPC and Section 4 of POCSO Act are in respect of the sexual assault.
An alternative punishment is provided under Section 42 of POCSO Act.
Such being the case,
convicting the appellant both for Section 376 of IPC and Section 4 of POCSO Act and sentencing separately, is not correct.
Therefore, I am of the view that the judgment of conviction and the order of sentence passed by the trial Court calls for interference and liable to be is set aside.

34. Accordingly, I pass the following order:
 (i) The appeals are allowed.
